title: The Golden Fishing Net of Agra (TA)
summary: A fisherman rises to become a wealthy minister and keeps a golden net in his palace. Birbal explains the profound memory behind the treasure. [TA]
full_text:
A humble, honest river fisherman named Sadhu rose through dedication, courage, and talent to become an imperial tax commissioner under Emperor Akbar. He lived in a fine mansion and received a handsome salary.

Envious courtiers noticed that in the center of his lavish reception hall, Sadhu had mounted an old, frayed, mud-stained hemp fishing net inside a glass cabinet lined with velvet and gold leaf.

The courtiers mocked him: 'Look at that peasant! He has become a high minister, yet he displays a filthy fishnet in his palace to insult the nobility!'

Akbar was curious and asked Sadhu in court: 'Commissioner, why do you keep a dirty old fishing net in a golden cabinet?'

Before Sadhu could speak, Birbal stepped forward with deep respect:

'Sire, allow me to honor Commissioner Sadhu's golden net.

'Many men who rise from humble poverty into royal wealth immediately become arrogant, look down upon the poor, and pretend they were born of kings.

'Sadhu keeps his old fishing net where he must gaze upon it every single morning before putting on his silk robes and signing tax decrees.

'The net reminds him: "Remember that you were once a hungry, barefoot fisherman on the muddy banks of the Yamuna, and that your power is a trust from the Emperor to serve the poor, not to oppress them!"

'That frayed net is the anchor of his humility, preserving his soul from the intoxicating poison of pride.'

Akbar was so moved by the explanation that he walked across the hall and embraced Commissioner Sadhu:

'Blessed is the empire whose ministers remember their humble origins! Would to God that all my courtiers kept their old plows and fishnets in their palaces!'

Akbar rewarded Sadhu with a jade seal, praising Birbal for defending the beauty of humility.
moral: நீதி மற்றும் வாழ்க்கை பாடம்: Wit beats power
